strings.title: Vanished on Opening Night
strings.hint: Follow the invoice. Who booked the truck a full day before the disappearance? Who 'lost' his access card exactly a week earlier?
strings.solvedText:
The offender: Ziad Al-Halabi — the artist and gallery partner.

Sara discovered that three paintings in her gallery were forgeries. Ziad was secretly selling the originals to repay his debts. She confronted him behind the curtain at 21:05 and gave him until the end of the reception to confess. He slipped a sedative into her glass and removed her in the 'wooden statue' crate whose transport he had booked a full day earlier — a planned abduction, not an improvisation. He removed the original painting to make it look like a theft.

Sara was found drugged but safe in the Studio Z. for the Arts warehouse in the industrial district, alongside the original painting and the forgery dossier she had assembled. The card supposedly 'lost a week earlier' was in Ziad's coat pocket.
strings.summary.text: At the height of Al-Mada Gallery's opening reception, its owner Sara Al-Ansari vanished. Her broken glass lay behind a curtain; The Heir, the gallery's most valuable painting, had been removed from its frame; and the painting storeroom door stood ajar. There was no blood, and nobody saw her leave. Her phone went silent at 21:35. Was it a theft that became an abduction, or a performance carefully staged by Sara herself?
strings.summary.photoCap: The exhibition hall after the reception was evacuated
strings.summary.victim.name: Sara Adel Al-Ansari
strings.summary.victim.note: Missing — search ongoing since the night of 14 January
strings.summary.timeline[1].l: Sara last seen inside the hall
strings.scene.address: Al-Mada Gallery — diplomatic district, main exhibition hall and storeroom
strings.scene.intro: A fast-acting sedative was found in the champagne glass behind the east-wing curtain. A faint drag mark leads toward the service corridor. The painting was hastily cut from its frame with a blade. The storeroom was opened with a card, without tampering — whoever did this knew the building well.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: Main hall — empty frame and markers 1 and 2
strings.scene.photos[1].cap: The glass behind the east-wing curtain
strings.scene.notes[0]: Glass containing fast-acting sedative residue behind the curtain
strings.scene.notes[1]: Ziad's card opened the storeroom at 21:18
strings.scene.notes[2]: Fire system recorded the service door opening at 21:26 for four minutes
strings.scene.notes[3]: A small truck left the service gate at 21:44
strings.evidence[0].title: The champagne glass
strings.evidence[0].desc: Bears Sara's lipstick and a fast-acting sedative. It fell without shattering completely. The sedative was added minutes before the fall.
strings.evidence[1].title: The empty frame
strings.evidence[1].desc: The frame of The Heir. The painting was hastily cut out with a sharp blade. Its insured value is two million riyals.
strings.evidence[2].title: Torn invitation and storeroom card
strings.evidence[2].desc: An invitation bearing the name of a guest who never checked in, and the storeroom card used at 21:18. The card is registered to Ziad Al-Halabi, who reported it 'lost' a week earlier.
strings.evidence[3].title: Sara's scarf
strings.evidence[3].desc: Her silk scarf carries traces of a luxury men's fragrance. The sample does not match the fragrances worn by those on the registered guest list.
strings.evidence[4].title: Fire system log
strings.evidence[4].desc: The storeroom service door opened at 21:26 for four minutes, then closed securely.
strings.evidence[5].title: Express shipping invoice
strings.evidence[5].desc: An advance booking, made a full day before the disappearance, to transport a 'heavy wooden statue' at 21:40. Paid by Studio Z. for the Arts.
strings.evidence[6].title: The office safe
strings.evidence[6].desc: 60 thousand is missing, withdrawn at 20:55 using assistant Lama's fingerprint under an authorization signed on the morning of the reception.
strings.suspects[0].name: Ziad Al-Halabi
strings.suspects[0].alibi: 'I never left the hall. I was welcoming critics all evening.'
strings.suspects[0].statement: Sara is like my younger sister in this world. We built Al-Mada together from nothing. I lost my storeroom card a week ago and told management verbally — ask Lama. Ibrahim Al-Mansour's talk of forgery is nothing more than blackmail by a bitter creditor. Last night, I sold three paintings at once. Why would I ruin the most successful night of my life?
strings.suspects[1].name: Lama Al-Harbi
strings.suspects[1].alibi: 'I spent most of the evening welcoming guests at the entrance.'
strings.suspects[1].statement: I withdrew 60 thousand from the safe with an authorization Sara signed that morning, to pay my mother's hospital debt. I had the paper and gave it to the investigator. I was crying in the corridor because Mr. Al-Mansour insulted me and threatened to shut the gallery down around us. Sara had been tense all week. She kept saying something about the paintings 'wasn't right.'
strings.suspects[2].name: Ibrahim Al-Mansour
strings.suspects[2].relation: The gallery owes him one million riyals
strings.suspects[2].alibi: 'I left at 20:30. My driver and your gate cameras can confirm it.'
strings.suspects[2].statement: Yes, I threatened to bring the gallery down. I bought two paintings from Ziad that my expert identified as criminally skillful copies. I came to give Sara one last chance: expose her partner herself, or I would expose them both to the entire art world. She arranged to show me 'the complete file' after the opening, then vanished before our meeting. I did not silence her. I was the one eagerly waiting to hear her speak.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Sami
strings.witnesses[0].statement: Around 21:05, I heard tense whispers between Sara and Ziad behind the east-wing curtain. I caught one sentence from her: 'Until the end of tonight… or I will speak.' Minutes later, Ziad asked me to take two glasses to the east wing.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Gate guard
strings.witnesses[1].statement: A small truck left through the service gate at 21:44 with an advance permit in an art studio's name. The driver showed all the paperwork, so I did not stop him. The permit had been issued a day earlier.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Dana
strings.witnesses[2].statement: Lama was crying in the corridor around 20:40 after speaking to Al-Mansour. Two days before the reception, Sara asked me something strange: 'Who would you trust to authenticate a painting… in complete confidence?'
strings.witnesses[3].name: Truck driver
strings.witnesses[3].statement: We loaded a very heavy wooden statue crate at the service door — heavier than any statue I have carried. A thin man in a coat received it, signed illegibly in blue ink and asked us to unload at a warehouse in the industrial district.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Missing-person report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body:
Assistant Lama Al-Harbi filed the report after all attempts to make contact and a search of the building failed.
Sara's description was circulated and the gallery sealed off.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Glass analysis
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body:
A fast-acting sedative, midazolam, in a dose reported to cause unconsciousness within minutes without a lasting effect.
A partial fingerprint on the glass stem does not belong to Sara.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Storeroom card and log examination
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body:
The card is registered to Ziad Al-Halabi and opened the storeroom at 21:18.
There is no official written report that it was lost. The claimed verbal report is unsupported.
strings.folders[2].name: Laboratory analyses
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Scarf fragrance analysis
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body:
A limited-edition luxury men's fragrance.
The exclusive distributor has an invoice for a bottle purchased a month earlier in Ziad Al-Halabi's name.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Painting authenticity report
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body:
Urgent examination of three exhibited paintings: highly accomplished forgeries with paint no more than a year old.
All three originals were secretly sold to overseas buyers during the past year.
strings.folders[3].name: Interviews
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Ziad Al-Halabi interview
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body:
Denied leaving the hall. Waiter Sami contradicts him: whispers behind the curtain at 21:05 and the request for two glasses.
Could not explain the shipping booking made a day earlier in his studio's name.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Lama Al-Harbi interview
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body:
Produced the withdrawal authorization Sara signed on the morning of the reception and the hospital payment receipt.
Her account is consistent with the entrance cameras.
strings.folders[3].docs[2].title: Ibrahim Al-Mansour interview
strings.folders[3].docs[2].body:
Confirmed leaving at 20:30, corroborated by gate cameras and his driver.
Handed over his expert's report on the two forged paintings and both purchase invoices.
strings.folders[4].name: Records
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Door system log
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body:
Storeroom opened at 21:18 with Ziad's card. Service door opened at 21:26 for four minutes.
No further opening before the police arrived.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Service gate cameras
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body:
A small truck leaves at 21:44 with an advance permit.
The camera angle does not cover the loading area, a blind spot known to gallery staff.
strings.folders[4].docs[2].title: Express shipping invoice
strings.folders[4].docs[2].body:
Advance booking dated 13 January, a full day before the disappearance, to transport a 'heavy wooden statue.'
Paid by Studio Z. for the Arts. Destination: a warehouse in the industrial district.
strings.folders[5].name: Classified files
strings.folders[5].docs[0].title: Complete forgery dossier
strings.folders[5].docs[0].body:
A dossier Sara secretly compiled was found in her private email: comparison photographs, a preliminary expert opinion and a record of Ziad's overseas sales.
She intended to confront him on opening night and give him a chance to confess, as the waiter partly overheard.
strings.folders[5].docs[1].title: Warehouse raid memorandum
strings.folders[5].docs[1].body:
Raid on Studio Z.'s warehouse in the industrial district:
Sara was found sedated and stable, alongside the original painting The Heir and the wooden shipping crate.
Ziad Al-Halabi was arrested at the scene.
strings.reports[0].title: Preliminary report
strings.reports[0].author: Lead investigator — Major S. Al-Omari
strings.reports[0].body:
Theft alone does not explain the sedative in the owner's glass. Voluntary disappearance is inconsistent with the drag mark.
The most likely explanation is a planned abduction by an insider who knows the doors, blind spots and system timings.
strings.reports[1].title: Gate camera report
strings.reports[1].author: Surveillance team
strings.reports[1].body:
Al-Mansour's departure at 20:30 is confirmed.
The truck left at 21:44 with an advance permit issued a day before the incident — the key timing clue in this case.
strings.reports[2].title: Financial unit report
strings.reports[2].author: Financial investigations unit
strings.reports[2].body: Ziad Al-Halabi's debts approach 900 thousand. Unexplained cash deposits over the past year match the dates on which the originals were sold and replaced with forgeries.
strings.notes[0].text: No blood: sedation and quiet transport. Who knows the blind spots?
strings.notes[1].text: Shipping permit issued a day before the disappearance — a planned abduction
strings.notes[2].text: Ask the insurer about The Heir
